title: 第四十六章 鏖战飞鹰第四十五章 飞鹰尽扫
content_zh:
飞鹰堡建在断崖上。
三面绝壁，一面通山。城墙用巨石垒成，缝隙里填着干透的黄泥，被风沙打磨了几十年，棱角都钝了。
萧无恨站在堡门前，手握着剑。
身后是刚刚扫平的十二座哨台。烽火还在烧，黑烟升上去，被风吹散，像墨滴进水里。
他一个人来的。
慕容小雪留在山下的镇子里。她说这种仗不需要两个人打，她去了反而让他分心。
萧无恨没有争辩。
她说得对。
他的剑已经痊愈了。不是那种勉强能用的痊愈，是从骨子里透出来的通透。从洞府出来后，他花了些时日把体内最后一点淤血化尽，经脉像被水洗过一样，剑气流转再无阻滞。
他还没有真正全力出过剑。
杀欧阳长青那一战，他只出了七分力。不是不想出全力，是欧阳长青的邪功已经撑不住他全力一击了。上册合一的白骨内功确实霸道，但在他的剑意面前，那种霸道像一块冻硬的石头，看着硬，敲开了里面全是裂纹。
他用了三剑。
第一剑破开白骨罡气，第二剑削断欧阳长青的右臂，第三剑穿胸而过。
三剑，欧阳长青倒在他面前。
金陵的势力在他死后第三天就散了。墙倒众人推，那些被他压服的门派第一个反水，瓜分了他的地盘和财富。萧无恨没有拦，也没有参与。他等了几天，等风声落定，等金陵的乱局平息，等那些想捡便宜的人捡够了，才动身往西北来。
因为骆一禾还在。
飞鹰堡还在。
四大宗主，已经倒了两个。慕容秋死在欧阳长青手上，欧阳长青死在他剑下。上官复向来滑溜，战后第一时间收缩势力，退回中原腹地，摆出一副两不相帮的姿态。
只有骆一禾不退。
他不肯降，也不肯逃。他把飞鹰堡的城门关死，把所有弟子召回堡内，摆出了死守的架势。

萧无恨知道他在等什么。
等他自己送上门来。
所以他来了。
风从崖顶灌下来，卷着沙砾打在脸上，生疼。
萧无恨眯了一下眼，迈步走向堡门。
门没关。
两扇厚重的铁门敞开着，门洞里面黑漆漆的，像一张嘴。
他走进去。
穿过门洞，是一个大得惊人的演武场。地面铺着青砖，被踩得坑坑洼洼，边角积着沙土。演武场四周立着兵器架，刀枪剑戟都有，但插得乱七八糟，像主人根本没心思打理。
正前方，是一座高大的石殿。
殿前站着一个人。
骆一禾。
他穿了一身黑色的劲装，袖子卷到肘弯，露出两条布满旧伤的手臂。他的手掌比常人大一圈，指节粗壮，指甲修剪得很短，一看就是练掌法练了几十年的人。
他没有说话，只是看着萧无恨。
萧无恨也没有说话。
两个人隔着演武场对视。
风从他们之间穿过去，卷起几粒沙。
骆一禾抬起右手。
殿内和两侧的廊道里同时走出人来。一个，两个，三个，越来越多，最后演武场上站了十个人。都是四十岁上下的汉子，个个手掌厚实，太阳穴鼓着，呼吸沉稳绵长。
十个人，十双眼睛，全部盯着萧无恨。
content_en:
Flying Eagle Castle is built on a cliff.
There are cliffs on three sides and a mountain on one side. The city wall is made of huge stones, and the gaps are filled with dry yellow mud. It has been polished by wind and sand for decades, and the edges and corners have become blunt.
Xiao Wuhen stood in front of the fort gate, holding a sword in his hand.
Behind him are the twelve sentry towers that have just been leveled. The beacon fire was still burning, and the black smoke rose up and was blown away by the wind, like ink droplets falling into the water.
He came alone.
Murong Xiaoxue stayed in the town at the foot of the mountain. She said that this kind of battle does not require two people to fight, and her presence only distracted him.
Xiao Wuhen did not argue.
She's right.
His sword was healed. It's not the kind of healing that can barely be used, it's the kind of transparency that comes from the bones. After coming out of the cave, he spent some time to eliminate the last bit of congestion in his body. His meridians seemed to have been washed by water, and the sword energy flow was no longer blocked.
He has never really used his sword at full strength.
In the battle to kill Ouyang Changqing, he only contributed seven points. It's not that he doesn't want to use all his strength, it's that Ouyang Changqing's evil skills can no longer withstand his full blow. The White Bone Internal Kung Fu in the previous volume is indeed overbearing, but in the face of his sword intent, that overbearingness is like a frozen stone. It looks hard, but when it is knocked open, there are cracks inside.
He used three swords.
The first sword broke through the bones, the second sword cut off Ouyang Changqing's right arm, and the third sword pierced the chest.
With three sword strikes, Ouyang Changqing fell in front of him.
Jinling's power dispersed on the third day after his death. When the wall fell and everyone pushed back, those sects that he had subjugated were the first to rebel and divide his territory and wealth. Xiao Wuhen did not stop or participate. He waited for a few days, for the news to settle, for the chaos in Jinling to subside, and for those who wanted to take advantage of it, before he set off to the northwest.
Because Luo Yihe is still there.
Flying Eagle Fort is still there.
Two of the four major sect masters have fallen. Murong Qiu died at the hands of Ouyang Changqing, and Ouyang Changqing died under his sword. Shangguan Fu has always been slippery. After the war, he immediately shrunk his power and retreated to the hinterland of the Central Plains, assuming a posture of not helping each other.
Only Luo Yihe refused to retreat.
He refused to surrender or escape. He closed the gate of Flying Eagle Castle, called all his disciples back into the castle, and put on a defensive posture.
Xiao Wuhen knew what he was waiting for.
Wait for him to deliver it to your door.
So here he is.
The wind poured down from the top of the cliff, carrying gravel and hitting my face, which was painful.
Xiao Wuhen narrowed his eyes and walked towards the castle gate.
The door is not closed.
Two heavy iron doors were open, and the door was dark inside, like a mouth.
He walked inside.
Passing through the doorway is an astonishingly large martial arts arena. The ground was paved with blue bricks, which had been trampled into pits, and sand accumulated in the corners. Weapons racks were erected around the martial arts arena, including swords, guns, swords and halberds, but they were placed in a mess, as if the owner had no intention of taking care of them.
Directly ahead is a tall stone palace.
There was a man standing in front of the hall.
Luo Yihe.
He wore a black suit with his sleeves rolled up to the elbows, revealing two arms covered with old injuries. His palms were larger than those of ordinary people, with thick knuckles and short nails. It looked like he had practiced palm skills for decades.
He didn't speak, just looked at Xiao Wuhen.
Xiao Wuhen didn't speak either.
The two people looked at each other across the martial arts arena.
The wind passed between them, picking up a few grains of sand.
Luo Yihe raised his right hand.
People walked out of the hall and the corridors on both sides at the same time. One, two, three, more and more, and finally there were ten people standing on the martial arts field. They are all men in their forties, with thick palms, bulging temples, and steady and long breathing.
Ten people, ten pairs of eyes, all stared at Xiao Wuhen.
